messages:
inc-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected on continuous-batching path (hosted/generate-stream) in us-west2. p95 ~ 220ms -> 820ms, p99 ~ 380ms -> 2400ms. Streaming stalls reported, some clients saw partial streams then connection reset. Paging oncall.
alex: seeing same in dashboard. spike started ~2387654280. streaming stalls correlate with kv cache eviction logs. adding Maya + Sam to triage.
maya: oncall ack, checking batcher telemetry now. which queues are hot?
sam: I can pull logs. running quick query on batcher metrics
sam: query: `sum(rate(batcher_processing_time_ms_bucket[1m])) by (queue,seqlen_bin)` shows tail for seqlen_bin=short+long-mix high for queue=batcher-main
lia: I see higher batching latency and increased cache misses on KV store. eviction rate jumped around start time: `kv_evict/s 0 -> 450`.
alex: interesting — evictions could be invalidating KV prefixes that streaming uses for prefix caching, causing recompute of KV entries and blocking stream progress. eng-ml, any model-side changes deployed recently to KV usage patterns?
eng-ml: no model change in the last 48h. but recent traffic shift: big customer A started sending many short+very-long sequences interleaved (bursting), which could amplify mixed-seq batching behavior.
maya: could be mixed sequence lengths leading to batch padding amplification + KV churn. two angles: scheduling fairness and KV backpressure. immediate mitigations?
sam: mitigation proposal 1: reduce max_batch_size from 48 -> 24 for streaming route to shorten queuing time. quick config patch ready.
priya: mitigation 2: enable preemptive-shed policy for long sequences so short requests aren't starved.
lia: mitigation 3: throttle eviction pressure by increasing kv max_entries temporarily, or slow down eviction worker. that requires infra change to kv config.
ops-bot: deploy pipeline triggered by alex: `infra apply --target=batcher-config --vars max_batch_size=24 --env us-west2` (status: queued)
alex: while deploy is queued, we should open a fallback route for heavy customers: route-heavy -> dedicated-lowlatency pool (if capacity). Priya, can you check dedicated pool spare capacity?
priya: checking... dedicated us-west2 has ~12% spare GPU RPS headroom. can route up to 40% of heavy customer A traffic.
sam: I recommend we route heavy traffic first, then apply batch_size reduction, then tune KV evict. order: reroute -> patch batcher -> tune kv.
maya: agreed. reroute requested. Priya, please take action and post confirmation here.
priya: reroute in progress. command: `routerctl reroute --from=hosted/generate-stream --to=dedicated/lowlatency --filter=customer:A --percent=40` (done). traffic shifting: +8% in last 30s.
sam: seeing immediate drop in p95 for hosted route down to ~350ms. p99 still high ~1500ms but trending down.
alex: continue with batcher config change. infra deploy started.
ops-bot: infra apply completed: batcher max_batch_size=24 (us-west2). rollout id: r-2026-03-15-001. No errors.
maya: patch live. telemetry shows queueing delay reduced, p95 ~210ms, p99 ~900ms. still higher than baseline but improving.
eng-ml: some streams still stall when KV misses coincide with large batches. Next step is to increase kv.max_entries from 200k -> 500k for the cluster to reduce evictions. Ops/infra approval required.
alex: approve kv increase for hotfix window. Priya coordinate with infra.
priya: filed infra ticket #INF-7842, change window scheduled for 5m. applying now.
ops-bot: kv config change applied: kv.max_entries=500000 (rolling restart of 3 nodes). Progress logs attached.
sam: after kv bump, eviction rate fell to ~12/s. p99 now ~320ms, p95 ~200ms. streaming stalls count dropped to 3 from ~42 in last 15m.
lia: customer-impact: Customer A saw ~2% errors (aborted streams) during the 8-minute window. Support lead notified and we should send a summary.
alex: good. action items: 1) keep reduced max_batch_size for 2h then gradually ramp to baseline with traffic shaping tests. 2) implement scheduling fairness change (short-first queue) in next release. 3) add KV eviction alarm and circuit that reduces batch_size automatically when eviction > threshold. 4) postmortem if customer impact >1% errors (we crossed).
maya: I'm going to run a quick A/B simulation to tune batch_size vs throughput across mixed-length traffic. will post results in this thread.
sam: logs and quick debug snippet (if useful):
```
REPRO TIP: simulate mixed workload with wrk: 
wrk -t4 -c200 -d60s http://hosted/generate-stream -s scripts/mixedlen.lua
metrics: batcher_queue_ms, kv_miss_rate, stream_bytes_sent
```

eng-ml: follow-up: we'll add per-customer routing heuristics that detect bursty mixed-length patterns and auto-isolate them to dedicated pools.
priya: support notified, CS will reach out to Customer A with an incident summary. No SLA credit decision yet; will escalate if they ask.
alex: handoff: I'll be primary for next hour, Maya will follow for deeper fixes. Sam, please prepare an ops runbook entry for rapid kv-throttle + batch_size rollback.
sam: working on runbook now, will attach link when done.
maya: preliminary A/B: lowering batch_size to 24 restored p99, but reduced throughput ~6%. tradeoff acceptable short-term.
eng-ml: also note model cache eviction sensitivity differs by model size; will annotate models in catalog to help routing decisions.
lia: closing loop: monitoring shows stable for 10m post-changes. I'll watch for any resurgence and set alert suppression for noisy alarms.
alex: thanks team. I'll leave this thread open until 2h post-stable. TL;DR: root cause = mixed-seqlen traffic causing batching padding amplification + KV eviction spikes -> streaming stalls. Mitigations: rerouted heavy customer, reduced batch_size, increased kv capacity. Customer impact: brief stream aborts for customer A (~2% errors).
